previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of recurrent hyperkalemia was admitted for weakness, dizziness, and paresthesias. She had recently started baclofen for muscle spasms and took two 10mg doses before experiencing prolonged sleep and new neurological symptoms. In the emergency department, her potassium was 6.7 mEq/L (non-hemolyzed), prompting treatment with calcium gluconate and urgent hemodialysis. Her symptoms were attributed to both hyperkalemia and the sedative effects of baclofen combined with Dilaudid. She underwent multiple dialysis sessions, with potassium normalizing to 4.8 mEq/L. A right heart catheterization revealed improved pulmonary pressures, leading to an increase in her dry weight goal by 2kg to prevent excessive fluid removal. An ultrasound of the left leg showed no deep vein thrombosis despite tenderness. Due to persistent dizziness and safety concerns at home, she was discharged to an extended care rehabilitation facility with follow-up planned with neurology and instructions to monitor weight and INR.
problems: Adverse effect of antiparkinsonism drugs and other central muscle-tone depressants

Brief Hospital Course:
On ___, Ms. ___ was admitted to the gynecology service 
for treatment of R vulvar cellulitis after an office I&D of 
vulvar sebaceous cysts c/b cellulitis, failing outpatient 
management with Bactrim. 

*) Vulvar Cellulitis 
Upon admission, she was afebrile, VSS. She had no leukocytosis 
or bandemia. Her exam was notable for significant erythema, 
tenderness, and induration along the R vulva, no fluctuance was 
palpated. Given her h/o VRE and complex past medical history, 
infectious disease was consulted who recommended initiating 
vancomycin and unasyn. Pt tolerated both antibiotics well. 

On HD#2, upon clarifying her penicillin allergy (itchy rash), pt 
was transitioned to vancomycin and levaquin, with plan to screen 
for MRSA (nasal and rectal) and discontinue vancomycin if 
negative (results pending at the time of discharge). In 
addition, although erythema improved, repeat exam was notable 
for possible fluctuance. An ultrasound was performed which did 
not show evidence of an underlying drainable abscess. 

On HD#3, her exam was improved with no erythema and decreased 
induration and improved pain. She continued to be afebrile with 
no leukocytosis. 

*) ESRD/HTN 
Renal was consulted to continue pt's hemodialysis while 
inpatient and to assist with ABX dosing. Pt underwent scheduled 
dialysis on HD#1 and HD#3. Pt was continued on sevelamer and 
calcitriol. Her admission Cr was elevated to 7.6 and she was 
hyperkalemic to 5.6 which improved after hemodialysis to 3.1 and 
3.7, respectively on HD#2. 

*) Thrombotic microangiopathy/History of LUE DVT - Her admission 
INR was 1.0. Coumadin had previously been held when pt had 
undergone office I&D procedure. Coumadin was restarted on HD#2 
given no drainable vulvar abscess seen on ultrasound. INR was 
rechecked on HD#3 and noted to be 1.1.

*) Chronic pain - pt was continued on home dose of dilaudid as 
well as lidocaine patches with pain well controlled.
*) Pulmonary HTN - pt was continued on macitentan and sildenafil
*) Seizure disorder - pt was continued on lamotrigine without 
any seizure activity during this admission
*) Migraine headaches - pt was continued on fioricet and 
meclizine as needed.
*) GERD - pt was continued on omeprazole and ranitidine. 
*) OSA - pt was continued on CPAP 

By HD4, her vulva exam was significantly improved with no 
erythema, minimal induration, and decreased tenderness. She was 
tolerating a regular diet, voiding spontaneously, ambulating 
independently, and pain was controlled with oral medications. 
She was then discharged home in stable condition with outpatient 
follow-up scheduled, and plan to continue vancomycin and 
levaquin for 14 days total, with plan to discontinue vancomycin 
if MRSA screens return negative.

Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the gynecology service for evaluation and 
treatment of vulvar cellulitis. You have recovered well and the 
team believes you are ready to be discharged home. Please call 
Dr. ___ office with any questions or concerns. 
Please follow the instructions below.

Cellulitis:
* Please continue all antibiotics as instructed, and complete 
the whole course even when you start feeling better

General instructions:
* Take your medications as prescribed.
* Do not drive while taking narcotics.
* Take a stool softener such as colace while taking narcotics to 
prevent constipation.
* Do not combine narcotic and sedative medications or alcohol.
* Do not take more than 4000mg acetaminophen (APAP) in 24 hrs.
* You may eat a regular diet.
* You may walk up and down stairs.

Call your doctor for:
* fever > 100.4F
* severe abdominal pain
* difficulty urinating
* vaginal bleeding requiring >1 pad/hr
* abnormal vaginal discharge
* redness or drainage from incision
* nausea/vomiting where you are unable to keep down fluids/food 
or your medication
